# Fairstay Part A Claims (`fairstay-part-a-claims`)

Checks Medicare Part A skilled nursing claims before they go out: missing or malformed PDPM HIPPS codes on revenue code 0022, days billed at the default ZZZZZ code, covered days that differ from the census, coinsurance days that differ from benefit days 21-100, missing or short qualifying hospital stays (occurrence span 70), claims crossing a month end and through dates in the future. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Part A Claims never submits claims; the biller does. Fairstay Part A Claims never changes MDS assessments.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-part-a-claims demo
npx -y fairstay-part-a-claims mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Riverbend Care Center Part A claims for March 2026, checked as of 2026-04-02. HIPPS codes are shaped like PDPM codes but are made up. Planted: R401 coinsurance days off by one (benefit days 16-46 have 26 coinsurance days, the claim says 11), R402 HIPPS with an SLP letter out of range (M) and a 2-day qualifying stay, R403 ten default ZZZZZ days, R404 a claim across the month end with a through date in April, R405 no 0022 line at all and no qualifying stay, R406 31 days billed but discharged on 27 March, R407 a 0022 line with no HIPPS.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `parta_check` | List problems on Part A SNF claims, claim by claim, before they are submitted. | runs |
| `parta_write_report` | Write parta-part-a.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and parta-part-a.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/parta). | runs |
| `parta_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `parta_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `parta_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `parta_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairstay Part A Claims never submits claims; the biller does. | refused |
| `mds_edit` | Fairstay Part A Claims never changes MDS assessments. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `parta_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `claims` (required) | Part A claim lines under --root (UB-04 / 837I export): claim, resident, statement from and through, revenue code, HIPPS, units, charges, occurrence span 70 dates, coinsurance days |
| `census` | Optional census under --root, to check covered days and coinsurance days |
| `prior_days` | Optional file under --root: Part A days each resident used earlier in the benefit period |
| `as_of` | Date the claims are checked on (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-part-a-claims inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Part A claim lines (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` (required) | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, ICN, Patient Control Number, PCN |
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `from` | date | Statement From, From, Service From, From Date |
| `through` | date | Statement Through, Statement Thru, Through, Thru, Service To, Thru Date |
| `revenue_code` (required) | text | Revenue Code, Rev Code, Rev, RC |
| `hipps` | text | HIPPS, HIPPS Code, Rate Code, HCPCS/Rates, HCPCS |
| `units` | number | Units, Days, Service Units, Covered Days |
| `charges` | amount | Charges, Total Charges, Line Charges, Amount |
| `qs_from` | date | Occurrence Span 70 From, OS 70 From, Qualifying Stay From, QS From |
| `qs_to` | date | Occurrence Span 70 Through, Occurrence Span 70 Thru, OS 70 Thru, Qualifying Stay Through, QS Thru |
| `coinsurance_days` | number | Coinsurance Days, Coins Days, Value Code 09 |

## Memory

`parta_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `parta_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `claim_note` | is shown with results for the billing team. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-part-a-claims": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-part-a-claims",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-part-a-claims -- npx -y fairstay-part-a-claims mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-part-a-claims tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-part-a-claims sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-part-a-claims inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-part-a-claims call parta_check '{"claims":"<claims>"}'
fairstay-part-a-claims eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-part-a-claims demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
